verdicts.why: beaconindex/beaconindex/assistant.py:31 uses (?!\S*\.beacon\.internal) after https?://, and \S* is unbounded, so putting .beacon.internal anywhere in the same non-space run (query, fragment) kills the match; the rule fails open even when guardrails mode is flipped to enforce (assistant.py:45).

settlement/reconcile.py:70-72 logs d.tenant_id and d.account with %s; those strings come straight from csv.DictReader rows at reconcile.py:45-46 with no validation or newline stripping, so a scheme-supplied field can forge log lines.

The 'public' default at warehouse-dbt/macros/apply_grants.sql:17 is unreachable in this tree: profiles.yml declares exactly three outputs (dev at line 8, ci at 20, prod at 32) and all three are keys of reader_by_target (apply_grants.sql:11-15), so target.name never misses.

harborlight-mobile/src/api/client.ts:70-75 retries against PROFILE.fallbackBase passing an empty pin array to send(), while the primary call at line 60-65 passes PROFILE.certificatePins (populated for production in src/config/env.ts:32-35).

AndroidManifest.xml:62-66 declares AttachmentProvider exported=true with grantUriPermissions and no android:permission/readPermission, and AttachmentSync.kt:34-38 builds the File from uri.lastPathSegment with no canonicalisation, so the caller's URI picks the path.

settlement/consumer.py:69-72 HMACs only entry['body'], then line 75 takes msg['type'] from the unsigned stream field, and consumer.py:89 selects the handler from that value, so the routing field is outside the signature.

settlement/retry.py:43 calls handlers._apply_payout(msg) directly on every dead-letter entry: it bypasses consumer.decode() (the only signature check, consumer.py:69) and _require_scope (handlers.py:27), which _apply_payout explicitly assumes the caller already did (handlers.py:43).

consumer.js:28 wires ledger.post.v1 to makeLedgerPostingHandler without the idempotency object that the payout handlers get on lines 29-30, and handlers/ledgerPosting.js:23 calls applyPosting with no key or dedupe, so an at-least-once redelivery re-applies the credit.

routes/attachments.ts:38-63 reads workOrderId from the form and inserts it with actor.orgId, never querying work_orders to confirm the order belongs to the caller's org; the only authorization is requireAuth on the caller (src/index.ts:28).

playbooks/site.yml:24-28 re-downloads from stanchion_artifact_mirror with no checksum: key (the primary download at roles/app/tasks/main.yml:26 does have one), unpacks at site.yml:30-36 under the become=root default in ansible.cfg:15-18, and the rescue triggers precisely on the role's failure.

consumer.js:30 registers payout.release.v2 but src/schema.js:27-52 defines EVENT_SCHEMAS only for ledger.post.v1 and payout.release.v1, and validatePayload returns null (= valid) when validatorFor finds nothing (schema.js:69-70).

src/index.ts:37 calls .listen(Number(process.env.PORT ?? 3000)) with no hostname, so Bun binds 0.0.0.0, while edge.conf:7-10 documents the upstream as loopback-only and src/auth.ts:19-28 derives the actor from X-Forwarded-Subject/Account headers the edge overwrites (edge.conf:44-46).

src/deeplink/router.ts:46 validates state.returnTo through assertAllowedRoute, but line 47 passes state.params — parsed from the same attacker-controlled link JSON at line 45 — into nav.navigate unchecked.

settlement/reconcile.py:56 writes the balance key with a raw redis SET from d.theirs_cents, which comes from int(row['closing_cents']) in the CSV (reconcile.py:47); it never goes through ledger.post_entry, whose negative-balance refusal is at ledger.py:65-69.

beaconindex/ingest.py:123 constructs the plain dataclass Document(**message['doc']) (defined without validation at ingest.py:54-61), so the queue path skips the DocumentIn tenant pattern, size limit and acl_groups wildcard rejection at ingest.py:28-51.

quarrystore/migrations/0007_case_notes.py:29-45 unconditionally inserts firm_demo and prn_demo in every environment; grep over the package finds no other reference to the demo firm, so the 'skipped by every production query filter' claim at line 27-28 has nothing behind it (session.py:34-49 filters by current_firm only, and not on principals at all).

warehouse-dbt/macros/mask_pii.sql:33 hashes customer_id concatenated with var('pii_policy_version'), whose value 'v3' is checked into dbt_project.yml:18, so the digest is unsalted in practice over a low-entropy id and is trivially recomputable.

Every link holds: config/default.json:21 sets signature mode 'warn' and signing.js:43-45 returns true unless mode is 'enforce'; consumer.js:60 therefore admits a forged entry; type payout.release.v2 has no schema (schema.js:27-52) so validatePayload passes; consumer.js:30 routes it to handlers/payoutRelease.js:28, which calls ledger.adjustBalance — no solvency check, no ceiling (ledger.js:59-65).

SessionStore.kt:62 declares tokenFor(host: String) and returns the same stored bearer regardless of host; the parameter is never read, so the API implies a per-host binding it does not implement (the host check actually lives in AuthInterceptor.kt:19).

quarrystore/search.py:34 interpolates needle into a single-quoted SQL literal inside text(); escape_like at search.py:13-17 escapes only % and _, never the quote character, so a term containing ' breaks out (contrast search_docket at line 51-56, which binds :needle).

ragsvc/tools.py:20-26 fetches any URL the model asks for with no scheme or host allow-list and returns 4000 chars of the body, ragsvc/app.py:117-121 feeds that back into the conversation, and any key holder (including the published demo key, settings.py:47) can steer the loop via the unconstrained history array (app.py:27, prompt.py:41-42).

beaconindex/chunker.py:23 only substitutes tags with a space and lines 24-26 collapse whitespace: text hidden inside markup survives as prose, and there is no NFKC/zero-width/bidi handling anywhere on the ingest path (ingest.py:66 calls chunk directly); retrieved text lands in the system prompt (assistant.py:110) while _screen only runs on the question (assistant.py:107).

The tree holds exactly five manifests — pulsegate-api/package.json:12-18 (^), tallyflow-consumer/package.json:12-18 (^), harborlight-mobile/package.json:11-18 (^), beaconindex/pyproject.toml:6-12 (>=), quarrystore/pyproject.toml:6-12 (>=) — and a find for package-lock/yarn/pnpm/bun/poetry/uv lockfiles returns nothing.

storage.ts:50-68 attaches an anonymous s3:GetObject policy when publicExports is set, and Pulumi.staging.yaml:9 and :12 set publicExports and replicateProdExports both to true, so the staging bucket that receives prod objects (storage.ts:70-89) is world readable.

storage.ts:42-48 derives all four public-access-block flags from !args.publicExports, so with Pulumi.staging.yaml:9 set to true all four are false, and storage.ts:51-67 adds the Principal '*' read policy while lines 70-89 accept replication from the prod export role.
settlement/reconcile.py:70-72 writes tenant_id and account into a single-line log record; both fields are unvalidated CSV columns read at reconcile.py:45-46, so embedded newlines forge entries.
routes/accounts.ts:75 declares members as t.Array(t.Object(...)) with no maxItems, and the handler at lines 65-71 loops one INSERT per row, so a single request drives an unbounded number of writes.

The uploader-chosen type is stored (attachments.ts:62) and echoed (attachments.ts:102), but the same handler sets Content-Disposition: attachment and X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff on lines 103-104, so the reflected type is never rendered inline and the CWE-434 harm the finding claims does not land.

settlement/consumer.py:69-72 compares the HMAC of the body field only; the type field is read separately at line 75 and is what HANDLERS.get dispatches on at consumer.py:89, so swapping payout for payout.reissue (handlers.py:107, which has no scope check) survives verification.

handlers/ledgerPosting.js:35 does interpolate p.currency, but consumer.js:28 routes only ledger.post.v1 to this handler and that type's schema constrains currency to the four-value enum at schema.js:8 (additionalProperties false, validated before dispatch at consumer.js:66-71), so no injectable value reaches the string.

routes/workorders.ts:123 gates PATCH on wo.orgId === actor.orgId only, while the list it mirrors narrows techs to their crews via visibleCrewFilter (workorders.ts:60-70, policy.ts:47-50), and requireRole (middleware/auth.ts:81) is imported by no route — grep finds only its definition.

src/lib/policy.ts:18-23 is a const object literal whose comment on lines 14-17 claims it is loaded at boot and refreshed nightly; grep shows crewSites is only read (policy.ts:40) and never assigned, so revoking a crew's site needs a redeploy.

src/api/endpoints.ts:37-41 ships LEGACY_ENDPOINTS including legacySupportImpersonate -> POST /legacy/support/impersonate, under the comment at lines 33-36 stating the gateway still answers these routes for old installs.

routes/accounts.ts:25 indexes the plain object literal SORT_COLUMNS (db.ts:17-21) with a caller-supplied string and only falls back on a nullish result, so sort=constructor / toString / valueOf resolves an inherited prototype member and hands it to sql.unsafe(orderBy) at db.ts:78.

exports.py:30-32, 45-47 and 65-67 write note bodies and summaries with csv.writer; QUOTE_ALL quotes the field but does not neutralise a leading =, +, - or @, and no formula prefix is applied anywhere in the module.

repository.py:86-91 asserts write permission against the `case` argument and then stamps redacted_at on the separately supplied `note`, with no check that note.case_id == case.id, so a note from a more sensitive matter can be redacted through a matter the caller may write.

entitlements.ts:16-24 declares seats and apiCallsPerDay per plan and entitlementsFor only returns them for display (routes/accounts.ts:31); grep across the project shows seatsRemaining (entitlements.ts:57) has no caller and no member-insert path consults seats (accounts.ts:49, 68).

The debug task at playbooks/rotate-secrets.yml:20-23 does lack no_log, but line 23 carries tags: [never, troubleshoot]; the Ansible `never` tag means it is skipped on every ordinary run and executes only when an operator explicitly asks for that tag, so the playbook does not print the password as the finding states.

iam.ts:92-108 builds the partner-analytics trust policy with Principal { AWS: '*' } and Action sts:AssumeRole, conditioned only on sts:ExternalId and aws:SecureTransport, so any AWS principal holding the external id can assume it.

iam.ts:67-76 builds every task role's assumeRolePolicy with Principal { Service: 'ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com' } and no Condition block at all — no aws:SourceAccount and no aws:SourceArn — for all four services in the loop at iam.ts:65.

storage.ts:98-104 sets blockPublicAcls and ignorePublicAcls true but blockPublicPolicy false (line 101) and restrictPublicBuckets false (line 103), leaving exactly the two policy-side protections off on the reports bucket.

Pulumi.staging.yaml:9 sets publicExports true, which drives the anonymous s3:GetObject policy and the all-false public access block in storage.ts:42-68, while line 12 sets replicateProdExports true, wiring in the prod replication policy at storage.ts:70-89.

src/auth.ts:99 encodes process.env.SERVICE_TOKEN_KEY ?? 'local-development-key' and signs the service JWT with it on line 106, so an unset variable silently yields a token signed with a key committed to the repository.

models/staging/stg_payout_events.sql:26 filters created_at > max(created_at) of the existing table (and models/marts/customer_pii_masked.sql:33 does the same on updated_at), so a row whose timestamp ties the current maximum is excluded on this run and on every later run.

beaconindex/ingest.py:110 returns bool(message.get('signature')) and a producer-name check — the signature value is never verified against anything — and the accepted message is turned into a raw Document at ingest.py:123, skipping DocumentIn including the acl_groups wildcard validator (ingest.py:38-44).

storage.ts:153-177 does describe a fully public bucket, but createLegacyArchive is never invoked: grep over the stack finds only its definition, and index.ts:7,45 imports and calls createStorage alone, so no such bucket is ever provisioned.

storage.ts:51 and storage.ts:73 each declare an aws.s3.BucketPolicy bound to exports_.id, and Pulumi.staging.yaml:9 and :12 make both branches active in staging; S3 keeps one policy per bucket, so whichever applies last wins.

roles/app/tasks/main.yml starts the app twice — the docker container on line 49-58 (published to 127.0.0.1) and the systemd unit installed at 86-103 and started at 105-110 — and that unit's EnvironmentFile (line 97) is app.env, which renders LISTEN_ADDR from group_vars/all.yml:19 as 0.0.0.0; ufw is applied only in the bastion role, which site.yml:2-6 runs on hosts: bastion.
exports.py:29-32 writes note.body into the CSV row with no leading-character neutralisation; csv.QUOTE_ALL at line 27 only quotes the field, which a spreadsheet strips before evaluating a leading =.

handlers/payoutRelease.js:28 moves money through ledger.adjustBalance, and ledger.js:59-65 is a bare upsert with no negative-balance refusal and no maxPostingCents check — both of which its sibling applyPosting enforces at ledger.js:9-14 and 25-28.

ragsvc/app.py:27 declares history as an array with maxItems only and no items schema, and prompt.py:41-42 copies turn['role'] and turn['content'] straight into the message list, so a caller can insert a role: system turn ahead of the question that drives the tool loop at app.py:101-121.

dim_customer.sql:42 only filters deleted_at is null on a full-rebuild table, and a grep of the whole dbt project for retention/expiry/delete/snapshot turns up no expiry mechanism at all — customer_pii_masked.sql:33 is incremental on updated_at, so rows it already holds are never removed.

AndroidManifest.xml:47-52 declares the autoVerify https intent-filter with <data android:scheme="https" android:pathPrefix="/r/"> and no android:host, so the path attribute is ignored and any https link matches, landing in DeepLinkRouter.kt:61-63 which loads the URL into the WebView that exposes the session bearer (ReportWebViewActivity.kt:96).

store.py:15 constructs QdrantClient(url=..., timeout=20) with no api_key, and config/beacon.yaml addresses every backing service over plaintext: the store at line 4, the embeddings endpoint at line 11 and the LLM gateway at line 16.

data.ts:59-67 creates the analytics replica with publiclyAccessible: true in the public subnet group (line 54-57), and data.ts:71-78 opens port 5432 on network.dbSecurityGroup — the same group the primary uses at line 41 — to cidrIpv4 0.0.0.0/0.

config/beacon.yaml:24-27 strips x-beacon-principal and x-beacon-tenant (plus the request id) but not x-beacon-groups, which acl.py:38 reads from the same request to build the principal's groups — and those groups are the ACL half of the retrieval filter at acl.py:47-52 and may_read at acl.py:55-59.

Only handle_payout consults idempotency.lookup before applying (handlers.py:80-88); handle_payout_cancel at handlers.py:91-104 posts a credit with no lookup, handle_payout_reissue at 107-111 calls remember without ever checking, and handle_refund at 114-127 has none — all four are reachable via the type field in consumer.py:26-31.

repository.py:127-132 ignores its principal argument entirely — no policy.assert_can_read, unlike schedule_export at line 121 — and hands case_id to exports.export_case_bundle, which opens its own plain Session(bind=engine) (exports.py:57) and dumps every note body and author for that matter; the CLI path at exports.py:93-94 reaches it with no firm scope set at all.

ragsvc/settings.py:47 sets demo_api_key to the literal 'demo-playground-key' with no os.getenv wrapper, unlike every other field in the dataclass, and app.py:56-57 grants a full Principal on that constant — rotating or disabling it requires a code change.

workorders.ts:186 does compile a template with new Function, but the value can never come from the caller: the route's query validator printQuery (workorders.ts:164-168) is .strict() over { format } only, so zValidator rejects a request carrying ?template=... with 400 before the handler runs, leaving line 185 to fall back to the DEFAULT_SHEET constant.
